problem: It says a backtracking recursive descent parser 'accepts any grammar'. That is false as written: a left-recursive grammar sends the parser into infinite recursion, and this same chapter says so in Section 3 and in the first exam trap. A student will trust the stronger sentence and skip removing left recursion.
fix: A backtracking parser can handle any grammar without left recursion, at the cost of rescanning tokens; the worst case is exponential. Left recursion must still be removed first, because the procedure calls itself before consuming any token.

problem: The condition 'A → α | β is predictive when FIRST(α) ∩ FIRST(β) = ∅' is stated without qualification. It is only sufficient when neither α nor β can derive ε; if one is nullable, the choice of that alternative must also be checked against FOLLOW(A).
fix: Add: when an alternative can derive ε, the parser picks it only when the lookahead is in FOLLOW(A); the disjoint-FIRST rule alone does not cover nullable alternatives. (Section 3 already mentions the FOLLOW check, so link the two.)
